notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates with blue letters (the blue is hard to see through the blur); government vehicles have green plates.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 shows either a car with a short three-ridged antenna, or a white car with a white left stripe and yellow right stripe and no antenna.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Drives on the right, unlike neighbouring Thailand.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Intricate, curvy script that looks more ornate than the similar-looking scripts of Thailand and Laos.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete ladder poles with indents and ridges, plus round concrete poles with small holes; simple wooden poles are rare.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Stone bollards with red-and-white stripes, or with a red top and white base holding a reflector.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Stone road markers with a white base and rounded red top, showing road number on the narrow side and a town and distance on the wide side.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows, the reverse of every other country in the region; bollards often replace them.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Dashed or solid yellow centre lines; outer lines are rare and white.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Many roads are unpaved; only main and urban roads are tarmac.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Wooden stilt houses with vertical plank walls, often dark red-brown, light blue or ochre with bright blue trim.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Orange or red tiled roofs with ridge ornaments, or plain corrugated metal.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Highly decorative Buddhist temples with ornamented roofs and Buddhist flags.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Ads for the local beers Angkor and Anchor are everywhere, plus blue ruling-party signs, sometimes with three politicians side by side.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A low-quality camera with a wide circular blur and brownish colours, found in the southwestern half.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The central plain is flat farmland dotted with villages; the northeast is less cultivated and slightly hilly.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The southwest has the most elevation, with hills, low mountains and dense forest inland.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sandy white soil is common around the capital and southeast of it.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Near the northern border a mountain ridge shows to the north and the soil is red.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Triangular bollards with red stripes appear on one southwestern highway and in two nearby national parks.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black-and-white bollards appear on only one road in the southwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rubber plantations exist in a belt northeast of the capital and in the far northeast.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bilingual signs with Chinese writing are common in the main port city.
